channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Body Acupuncture, Electroacupuncture, and Auricular Acupuncture in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs found that acupuncture significantly improved motor function in stroke rehabilitation (SMD=6.48; 95% CI=4.72-8.24; P<0.001) compared to controls, with electroacupuncture showing the greatest efficacy.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinical and neurophysiological determinants of response to contralesional low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation after stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (up to July 2026) found that contralesional low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (LF-rTMS) effectively improves post-stroke upper-limb function, with treatment effects modulated by baseline motor impairment and corticospinal tract integrity.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of exercise-based prehabilitation before total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: This systematic review and network meta-analysis of RCTs compared the effectiveness of different exercise modalities for prehabilitation before total knee arthroplasty (TKA), finding high-intensity resistance training and aerobic exercise to be potentially more effective than conventional interventions.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effects of different aerobic exercise intensities on exercise capacity, quality of life and mortality in individuals with coronary artery disease: systematic review and network meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and network meta-analysis investigated the comparative effectiveness of different aerobic exercise intensities in adults with coronary artery disease (CAD) on exercise capacity, quality of life, and mortality, suggesting varying benefits across intensities.
item.author: Sport Sci Health

item.title: Efficacy of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Stimulation Montages and Timing.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (N=419) found that active tDCS significantly reduced neurological deficits (WMD=-0.86, 95% CI: -1.38 to -0.34, P=0.001) compared to sham stimulation in acute ischemic stroke, but did not significantly improve motor function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Beyond the Diagnosis: An Integrated Perspective on Strategic Dosing in Neurologic Motor Rehabilitation. A Scoping Review and Collaborative Viewpoint.
item.description: A scoping review and collaborative viewpoint explored strategic dosing in neurologic motor rehabilitation, suggesting a mechanism-based framework for therapeutic reasoning, dosing, and longitudinal adaptation, noting a distinction between higher-intensity approaches for non-progressive conditions and conservative strategies for progressive conditions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of a Personalized Robot-Assisted Trunk and Lower Limb Rehabilitation in Patients with Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=40) found that adding individualized robot-assisted trunk-lower limb training to conventional rehabilitation significantly improved Functional Ambulatory Category (FAC) in chronic stroke patients at 3 months, compared to conventional rehabilitation alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 articles found that physical exercise may be effective for cognitive function in older adults with Alzheimer's disease, though optimal dosage for targeted outcomes remains unclear.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Foot-Targeted Rehabilitation for Pronation-Related Anterior Knee Pain: A Two-Phase Case-Control Study and Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Manual Therapy Versus Neuromuscular Training Each With Augmented Low-Dye Taping.
item.description: This study characterized functional and biomechanical differences in AKP patients with pronated feet and compared foot-targeted manual therapy and neuromuscular training with augmented low-dye taping against routine care, showing comparable short-term effectiveness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of In-Clinic Rehabilitation vs. Home-Based Telerehabilitation for Adults with MS in the Deep South: The TEAMS Cluster Randomized Trial.
item.description: The TEAMS cluster randomized trial found that a 12-week complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) program for adults with MS was similarly effective whether delivered in-clinic (DirectCAM) or at home via telerehabilitation (TeleCAM).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Optimal Exercise Modality and Dose for Blood Pressure Management in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Systematic Review with Bayesian Model-Based, and Dose-Response Network Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
item.description: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of RCTs evaluated the optimal exercise modality and dose for blood pressure management in middle-aged and older adults, systematically comparing effects across aerobic, resistance, and combined training.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Telerehabilitation Versus Conventional Rehabilitation on Motor Function and Activities of Daily Living After Stroke: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of four RCTs (N=226) found telerehabilitation to be non-inferior to conventional physiotherapy for improving motor function (Fugl-Meyer Assessment) and activities of daily living (Barthel Index) in stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Arm exercise training in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: An umbrella review synthesized findings on arm exercise training for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), confirming its role in pulmonary rehabilitation, although the specific level of evidence requires careful consideration of the included studies.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Development and psychometric validation of the shoulder problems assessment scale.
item.description: The 12-item Shoulder Problems Assessment Scale (SPAS), an activity-based patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) using a hierarchical stepwise yes/no format, was developed and psychometrically validated in a multicenter study of 415 patients to identify the first threshold of difficulty during daily activities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: More Than Just Arm Movement: Finger-Worn Accelerometers Provide a Valid and Sensitive Alternative to Wrist-Worn Accelerometers for Measuring Real-World Upper-Limb Performance in Stroke Survivors
item.description: This cross-sectional observational study (N=20) found that finger-worn accelerometers are a valid and sensitive alternative to wrist-worn accelerometers for measuring real-world upper-limb performance in stroke survivors.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: A grade-specific clinical prediction rule for independent walking after traumatic spinal cord injury.
item.description: A clinical prediction rule was developed using the National Spinal Cord Injury Statistical Centre dataset (2607 patients) to predict independent walking one year after traumatic SCI, identifying grade-specific predictors.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A systematic review of early neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers for post-stroke mobility prognostication.
item.description: A systematic review identified early neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers measured <14 days post-stroke that predict mobility outcomes up to 24 months, providing insights into prognostic capacity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial (n=50) found that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the elastic coefficient of the dermis at day 9, compared to 0% tension taping, in patients with limb oedema.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of six weeks of ankle stretching exercises on ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and anterior knee pain in children with ankle pronation: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A six-week ankle stretching exercise program significantly improved ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and reduced anterior knee pain in children with ankle pronation.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Differences in the Thoracolumbar Fascia Between Low Back Pain Patients and Healthy Individuals: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found significant differences in the thoracolumbar fascia characteristics between individuals with low back pain and healthy controls.
item.author: Sports Med - Open
